name: SAVI (STING-associated vasculopathy of infancy)
aliases: STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy

reference.source: Textbook of Autoinflammation / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A type I interferonopathy caused by gain-of-function mutations in TMEM173 (STING1), leading to constitutive STING activation
Presents in infancy with systemic inflammation, failure to thrive, and a severe cutaneous vasculopathy affecting acral sites
Skin disease produces violaceous, telangiectatic, and ulcerating lesions of the cheeks, nose, ears, and digits, sometimes progressing to acral gangrene and tissue loss
Interstitial lung disease with progressive fibrosis is a major and potentially fatal feature
A strong interferon signature in blood supports the diagnosis alongside genetic confirmation
Recurrent fevers, arthritis, and myositis may accompany the vascular and pulmonary manifestations
JAK inhibition targeting interferon signalling is the mainstay of therapy and can stabilise skin and lung disease
reference.pathophysiology: SAVI is caused by gain-of-function mutations in TMEM173 (STING1) that lock the STING protein in a constitutively active state. Persistent STING signalling drives sustained transcription of type I interferons independent of the usual cytosolic nucleic-acid triggers. The resulting interferon excess produces a small-vessel vasculopathy, particularly at cool acral surfaces, and progressive interstitial lung inflammation and fibrosis. This interferon-dominated mechanism underlies the systemic inflammation and provides the rationale for JAK inhibition to interrupt downstream interferon signalling.
additionalDifferentials: CANDLE syndrome and other type I interferonopathies
Neonatal lupus and systemic lupus erythematosus
Interstitial lung disease of other autoimmune cause
additionalInvestigations: Genetic testing for TMEM173 (STING1) gain-of-function mutations
High-resolution chest CT for interstitial lung disease and fibrosis
Autoantibody panel to help exclude systemic lupus and antiphospholipid syndrome
Pulmonary function testing where age permits
redFlags: Progressive interstitial lung disease with respiratory failure
Acral gangrene threatening loss of digits or facial tissue
Severe failure to thrive with unremitting inflammation
reference.prognosis: SAVI is a serious disease with substantial morbidity and mortality driven mainly by progressive lung fibrosis; JAK inhibition can stabilise disease but pulmonary and acral damage may be irreversible.
pitfalls: Mistaking acral vasculopathy for frostbite, cold injury, or primary vasculitis
Underestimating and under-monitoring the interstitial lung disease
Relying on corticosteroids alone rather than targeting interferon signalling
Delaying genetic testing and interferon signature assessment in an unwell infant
